entries.summary: A decision, a spec and a plan are embedded as roots with their subtree; they were not embedded.

migrate.affectedData: The embedding rows of every existing decision, spec and plan root: none exist, and no normal path creates one until the root or a line of its body is edited.
migrate.transformation: Queue each existing decision, spec and plan root for embedding.

entries.summary: The saved queries "Ready tasks", "Waiting on you", "Needs shaping" and "In progress" stop shipping: the rules and skills that read them carry the filter and run it as an ordinary search, and the skills that were attached to them are attached to nothing.

migrate.affectedData: The four query nodes under their fixed ids in every database created by an earlier build. Opening a database does not remove them: they stay, run, and are listed in the navigation as saved queries. The attached_to links from the five skills (Implementing a Task, Creating a Task, Answering a Question, Diagnosing a Bug, Instrumenting a Change) to them are removed on open where the user left the links alone, and kept and recorded as pending where the user changed them.
migrate.transformation: Delete each of the four query nodes whose definition the user did not edit; keep an edited one as the user's own query and record the shipped removal as pending for them to decide.

entries.summary: A new core subtype of ai-chat, ai-chat-acp, with session_status and session_id (local_only); an older database lacks it and seeding creates its schema on open.
An ai-chat-message may also sit under an ai-chat-acp chat: the registry's must_have_parent_of list gains ai-chat-acp, and the derived rule rows are written from the registry on open.

The ai-chat-message schema's declared parent list gains ai-chat-acp; an older database's stored schema node keeps the old list and stays valid, because a core type's rules come from the registry rows (see the registry entry) and nothing reads the stored declaration.
Three core subtypes of tool are added: tool-mcp, tool-rest and tool-cli, each with its binding fields. A database that does not hold them is seeded with them.

The tool base gains a local-only approved_binding field. A database created by an earlier build holds a tool schema without it, which the core-type comparison reports as a missing field, so that database is refused at open (a schema mismatch) until it is reset.

The tool base's enabled field becomes local-only. The core-type comparison does not read the classification, so this change alone would not be noticed in a stored schema; the database is refused at open for the approved_binding field (see tool-approved-binding-field), and a reset brings in the new classification.

migrate.affectedData: The stored tool schema node's enabled field in every database an earlier build created: it keeps local_only false. Such a database is refused at open until it is reset, because its stored tool schema also lacks approved_binding.
migrate.transformation: Set local_only on the enabled field of the stored tool schema; in practice, reset the database.

entries.summary: The ai-chat-message schema gains five optional fields that record one part of an ACP chat turn: part_kind, tool_call_id, tool_title, tool_kind and tool_status. A database created by an earlier build holds a message schema without them, which the core-type comparison reports as missing fields, so that database is refused at open (a schema mismatch) until it is reset.

The ai-chat-message schema gains a confirmation part kind and five optional fields that record a question put to the user before a remote tool call runs: confirmation_id and confirmation_digest (device-local), confirmation_status, confirmation_arguments and confirmation_credentials. A database created by an earlier build holds a message schema without them, which the core-type comparison reports as missing fields and a part_kind without the new value, so that database is refused at open (a schema mismatch) until it is reset.

The ai-chat-message timestamp field changes from system to core protection. The app writes a user's own message, timestamp included, so it is not a field only code maintains. A database created by an earlier build holds the message schema with system protection, which the core-type comparison reports as a difference, so that database is refused at open (a schema mismatch) until it is reset.

Every core schema gains a `customFields` list beside its `fields`: where a field a user adds to the type is declared, stored under its own name (ADR-112). It ships empty and is the user's. An older database holds no such list, which reads as an empty one, and the core-type comparison and the hash leave the list out.
